sonnet.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the wording of Paul's line (obedience leading to 'righteousness'). Nothing earlier lets a baker reason to that word over 'glory' or 'wisdom', so the pick is a guess at the line's wording.
sonnet.rule: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

sonnet.problem: Card 9 already showed that the believers 'became slaves to righteousness.' Card 11's right answer, 'Offer them in slavery to righteousness', repeats that same fact. The other two answers are easy to rule out, so the answer is effectively given away.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question. An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.
